newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israelis to face charges for beating Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Two Israelis to face charges for beating Arabs.

text.p: A Jerusalem court on Thursday ordered two Israeli policemen, caught on videotape beating Palestinians, held for another three days while police prepare criminal charges, an official said.
"Their remand was extended until Sunday," a justice ministry spokeswoman said.

The two paramilitary border policemen, Tsahi Shamaya, 19, and David Ben Abu, 20, were shown in an amateur video beating and kicking six Palestinians in the head and body after detaining them in Jerusalem without work permits.

The video, shot by a Palestinian from a nearby apartment last month and broadcast on Israeli television on Monday, embarrassed Israeli leaders and outraged Palestinians. It was later broadcast on television worldwide.
Members of a justice ministry department that investigates alleged misdeeds by policemen arrested the two on Tuesday. Israel Radio said they were likely to be charged with aggravated assault.

"This Israeli policy will return us back to the age of confrontation, total confrontation. This policy will lead only to the destruction of all that was achieved between the two sides, the Israeli and the Palestinian sides," Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo said on Thursday.

Palestinians have often complained of abuse by border policemen stationed throughout the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the incident and said it was rare.
